speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: WSQ frameworks are also validated and endorsed by industry representatives to help ensure continued relevance to industry needs.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Similarly, the MOE-funded Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs), that is, ITEs, polytechnics and the autonomous universities, also have systems in place to monitor and maintain teaching standards and the quality of their programmes.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They participate in external audits that ensure their processes and programmes are well-run.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In addition, they are validated by external review panels that assess the institutions' systems and teaching approaches.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will continue to monitor the quality of our appointed partners and training programmes.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: I do support and agree that the SkillsFuture programme is a good one and it should be one that is about broad-based learning and lifelong learning.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: However, fairly often, I do hear from constituents that some of these WDA courses that are provided for them do not adequately enable them to look for jobs subsequently.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: One of the reasons they were told was that some of the courses they had taken were insufficient and they needed to go for additional accreditation.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: The first question is: would the Ministry consider putting up some guidelines or criteria to say what are the relevant courses which are applicable for particular industries so that people would have better guidance on how to go for the relevant courses because there are a lot provided currently?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: The second question is with regard to quality and assurance: could the Acting Minister elaborate on the frequency of the cross-accreditation and how do the auditors regularly benchmark these against what is being provided out there in the market?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: About finding jobs for her constituents, it is an inter-play of many factors of which training is one; the person's attitude is one; how picky the employer is is also one.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: That is why, for many years now, with the CDCs and with NTUC under the Employment and Employability Institute (e2i), there have been many career coaches being trained and they have been in the job for many years.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: They coach jobseekers and advise them on what courses to take, which companies to go for.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: For companies that are more picky, over time, e2i and the CDCs would no longer consider them their clients.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: They work with employers who are more welcoming to different kinds of workers.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, it is many factors at play, of which training continues to be but one.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It is necessary but it is not sufficient.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If you have constituents or residents who need help, do feel free to approach the CDCs or e2i, which MOE works closely with.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As for the second question on quality and assurance, the Member asked how frequent the accreditation of courses is.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If a training provider has come up with a course which it thinks can help workers and students, it can come forth to WDA.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: WDA has quite a speedy and efficient course accreditation system.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I am quite new to this job and even I got to launch the SkillsFuture Credit Scheme, which goes to show the scheme is very new.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I would really like to invite NTUC and Labour Members of Parliament, if there are courses out there that the unions give feedback that these are helpful, do let us know.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The intention is to broaden as much as we can.
